runs.content: Occidental Petroleum (OXY) picked up at the previous close ($59.10) — pure-play E&P leverage to the weekend US-Iran Strait of Hormuz strikes and resulting oil-price spike (WTI ~$85.46), backed by a standalone Aug 5 beat-and-raise (EPS $2.40 vs. $1.88 est., record production, debt cut $1.5B to $11.8B, 8% dividend increase), chosen over XOM/HAL (less direct crude torque) and VLO (refining margins can compress on a fast crude spike). WMT was exited discretionarily (−7.82%, −$78) to keep the book at 35 open positions after OXY's entry — no mechanical stop-losses or signal exits on the other 34 continuing positions. Portfolio net P&L: +$2,775 (+5.34% on $52,000).

Broadridge Financial Solutions (BR) picked up at the previous close ($183.08) — wide-moat proxy/governance infrastructure at a ~28% discount to Morningstar's $255 fair value, fresh Q4 FY2026 beat-and-raise (Aug 4) plus a new 12% dividend increase and $1.5B buyback, chosen over Zoetis (a Burry long, but just cut FY26 guidance) and Hershey (already re-rated above fair value). CrowdStrike's own Thursday earnings beat lifted CRWD +20.5% in one session to +37.44% overall, now within ~9% of T2. JBHT was exited discretionarily (−11.73%, −$117) to keep the book at 35 open positions after BR's entry — no mechanical stop-losses or signal exits on the other 33 continuing positions. Portfolio net P&L: +$2,721 (+5.34% on $51,000).
